title: xDrip+ draining G5 transmitter batter
symptom: User reports rapid degradation of Dexcom G5 transmitter battery voltage and resistance after switching from a Galaxy S5 to a BLU Dash X2 phone. Transmitters are failing within weeks, with low battery warnings after about 24 days. User is not in native mode and has OB1 enabled.
cause: The thread does not establish a definitive root cause. Possible causes discussed include the phone causing connection drops, expired sensors drawing more battery, or an issue with xDrip's OB1 communication mode. One user suggests that not using G5 Native mode may lead to early transmitter death, and another speculates that preemptive restarts may be involved.
fix: No definitive fix is provided. Suggestions include trying native mode with a new transmitter, turning off preemptive restarts and restarting the sensor before day 9, or switching to a G4 transmitter with a bridge. The thread ends with a request to close the issue, implying no resolution.
evidence_quote: I suggest this path TO MITIGATE PROBLEM (if you have battery drainage) until fix: - turn Preemptive restarts OFF - day 9 (or earlier if more convenient): stop sensor, hard reset transmitter*, start sensor again
